repo_commit.message:
Release code, data, results, and project page for arXiv:2609.34460

When Does Structured Knowledge Help Neural Theorem Proving?
Sareh Nabi, Roland Vogl, Marzieh Nabi (Stanford University)

- MathAgent implementation: Explorer, Conjecturer, Prover, Integrator,
  Orchestrator; MathKG construction; benchmark evaluator with the Lean 4
  verifier
- MathKG node file (364 nodes) and released graph (9,434 typed edges)
- Per-problem results and run configurations of the 28 evaluation runs
  (Qwen3-8B/32B, Goedel-Prover-V2-8B/32B, Claude Sonnet 4.6 on miniF2F,
  PutnamBench, MathOlympiadBench)
- Scripts for the ablation runs
- Project page (Astro, in site/) with slides; Pages workflow builds from site/
- README, MIT license, CITATION.cff

entries.available_artifacts: Primary abstract/PDF and an Astro project-page repository; runnable theorem-proving or ACC search implementation not established from this tree.
entries.limitations: Paper claims code/data availability, while linked repository README identifies a project page. No released executable engine established by this recheck; no external code run. Paper benchmarks are not ACC results.
entries.harness_question: Does the context/method complementarity hypothesis justify adaptive lane selection? Existing untried code lanes remain more concrete evidence than importing a website.
entries.bounded_falsifiable_next_experiment: Use existing receipts to compare which completed lanes actually produced independently verified own-road improvements per selected row. Reject claims of universal benefit from adding context if none of the observed rows support them.
entries.action: Version already recorded; no new private lead message or owner notification.
